Companion Animal Travel Desk - Pet Travel Administration Purpose: This section sets the standards for handling companion animal travel requests with care, accuracy, and consistent oversight.

At Aurelia Skyways, the Companion Animal Travel Desk exists to support humane, calm movement planning for traveling companions while maintaining reliable service controls. I acknowledge past inconsistency risks and, on behalf of quality assurance, we are tightening expectations so every request is handled the same way, from intake to cabin monitoring. The handlers must use gentle handling practices and avoid stress escalation in all interactions, including preparation and transfer moments. The senior coordinator oversees daily service decisions to confirm that arrangements match the approved service design, and the cabin team monitors animals during flight to keep welfare safeguards active throughout travel.

For fee determination, each animal type must be recorded exactly and matched to the approved schedule maintained by the desk. Specifically for a bird, the fee to bring this animal is $145. Fees must be entered once and verified before release to the traveler documents workflow to prevent downstream confusion. Where the traveler provides prior paperwork, the desk must reconcile any wording differences while keeping the approved fee record intact and audit-traceable.

For crate sizing checks, the desk must confirm the crate can support safe movement and ventilation consistent with our standard handling approach. For a bird, the longest crate side is 60 cm, measured as the maximum length across the crate exterior. The desk staff must inspect the crate before acceptance, record the measurement only once, and ensure the crate condition is suitable for the journey. If any mismatch is identified, the desk must stop processing and route the matter to the senior coordinator for resolution so cabin staff receive equipment that aligns with welfare expectations.

Throughout the process, the desk must maintain professional communication and accurate documentation, including clear instructions for travelers on preparation steps. If Andre Nguyen or Khalil Costa (travelers) request guidance and Mia (a pet) requires special attention, the desk must still apply the same verification steps and recording standards, with no relaxation of crate and fee checks. The desk may provide reassurance, but it must not alter any approved values or inspection results.

For compliance questions or exceptions review, contact the senior coordinator.
